title: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on Eleanor, heiress to Aquitaine, who married the future Louis VII of France in this cathedral in 1137. She later married Henry II of England, and Bordeaux passed to the English crown for 300 years.

title: The Black Prince
episode: Hundred Years' War: The Black Prince (Part 3)
description: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on Edward, the Black Prince, who brought the captured French king to Bordeaux after Poitiers in 1356 and later ruled Aquitaine from the city. His son, the future Richard II, was born here.

title: The 1855 classification

description: Wine writer Jane Anson on the ranking of Bordeaux wines drawn up by the city’s brokers for the Paris world’s fair of 1855, mostly by price. It is still in use, almost unchanged. The brokers worked from the Chamber of Commerce on this square.

episode: Bordeaux: Part II The Dutch and the Medoc
place: Musée du Vin et du Négoce, Chartrons
description: How Dutch merchants in the 1600s drained the marshes of the Médoc, north of the city, which became the source of Bordeaux’s most famous wines. Foreign merchants settled in the Chartrons, the quarter where this wine trade museum stands.

title: Montaigne
place: Statue of Montaigne, Place des Quinconces
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on Michel de Montaigne, born near Bordeaux in 1533, who retired at 38 to write what he called essays, or attempts, about himself and everything else. He also served two terms as mayor of Bordeaux.

title: The Girondins
description: Historian Mike Duncan on June 1793, when the Paris crowd forced the arrest of the Girondins, a moderate faction of the revolution named after the Gironde, the region around Bordeaux. Many went to the guillotine. Their monument stands on the Quinconces.

episode: Short Stuff: Aristides de Sousa Mendes
place: Statue of Aristides de Sousa Mendes
description: In June 1940, as refugees poured into Bordeaux ahead of the German army, Aristides de Sousa Mendes, the Portuguese consul, defied his government and issued thousands of visas. Portugal ended his career for it.

title: The Papon trial
description: Maurice Papon, a senior official in Bordeaux under the Vichy regime, signed orders that sent more than 1,500 Jews to the camps. He went on to a long career and was tried here only in 1997 and 1998, the longest trial in French history.

title: Goya
description: A discussion of Francisco de Goya and his unflinching art. Goya left Spain in 1824 to escape its absolutist king and spent his last years in Bordeaux, where he died in this house in 1828.
